title: Prove the sharp five-qubit Clifford tensor threshold T(5) = 15
body:
The full projective five-qubit Clifford tensor alphabet first becomes linearly independent over the complex numbers at **width 15**. At width 14 exactly two representation blocks are missing, giving nullity **6,954,742,423,552**. At width 15 all 198 odd-sector blocks occur. Together with #7803 this places the minimum raw Gaussian-dyadic splitting width between 15 and 17 inclusive.

The exact calculation uses the ordinary symplectic table and both orthogonal stabilizers. A separate embedding count recovers all three fixed-space histograms and checks two trace moments of the full Gram matrices. An optional second calculation from the original CTblLib archive verifies all 715 width-specific multiplicities in a certified finite field. The seven-pair seed from #7803 has a fixed vector in each ordinary irreducible, leaving odd-characteristic splitting as the next question.

All six registered Python 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and from the read-only, Git-free export. The two direct archive checks also passed. The contribution uses the ATLAS tables distributed with Thomas Breuer's CTblLib 1.3.11 and the earlier Clifford results of alephnan, Ali Romman, MatShep, Nick Petalas and apoursh.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-five-qubit-threshold
```

Committed bytes, source history, executable modes and export inventory passed the repository checks. Prepared by apoursh with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The selected conditional multiplication exponent remains unchanged.
